title: Lancelot, Guinevere and the Round Table
subtitle: Camelot and its fall
subject: mythologie
description: Arthur, Lancelot, Guinevere: the greatest legend of the Western Middle Ages. An ideal of chivalry destroyed by forbidden love.

hero.hook: The best knight in the world loves the king's wife. Camelot will not recover.

blocks.text: The legend of King **Arthur** and his knights of the **Round Table** is the great mythological cycle of the Western Middle Ages. We call it the **Material from Brittany**: a mixture of vague history, Celtic folklore and Christian morality.

At the heart of the story, a very human tragedy: the forbidden love between **Lancelot**, the best knight, and Queen **Guinevere**, Arthur's wife. This love, celebrated as perfection, becomes the poison that brings down **Camelot**.

sections.title: At the sources of myth: between history and Celtic folklore

blocks.text: No single author. Between the 6th and 15th centuries, stories accumulate. Behind Arthur, we see a Breton warlord, perhaps named **Arturus**, who would have resisted the Saxons after the departure of the Romans. Around him grow **Merlin**, the fairies, the magic swords.

blocks.caption: Arthur draws the sword from the rock: the sign of the rightful king.

blocks.text: A 13th-century “Round Table” still hangs in Winchester Castle, England. Henry VIII had it painted to link himself to Arthur.

During , only the true king can pull **Excalibur** from the rock or anvil. Crowned in Camelot, Arthur founded the **Round Table**. Its circular shape abolishes hierarchy: around it, each knight is the equal of his neighbor, including the king. [[the ordeal of the sword]]

sections.title: The quest for the Grail and spiritual mutation

blocks.text: Little by little, the fighting gives way to a spiritual quest: the **Holy Grail**. A magical dish in old Celtic texts, it became the chalice of Christ in the 12th century. Inner purity matters as much as strength.

blocks.caption: The quest for the Grail transforms the Round Table into a spiritual adventure.

blocks.text: The word "grail" came from ancient French and initially designated a large dish for serving meats, not a precious cut.

At the table, the  awaits the predestined knight. Only **Gilead**, **Perceval** and **Bohort** reach the Grail. **Lancelot of the Lake**, “best knight in the world”, fails: his love for Guinevere makes him unworthy of the divine vision. [[Perilous Siege]]

sections.title: Guinevere's betrayal and the tearing of order

blocks.text: The love of Lancelot and Guinevere embodies : the knight puts himself at the service of his lady. But Guinevere is the overlord's wife. The betrayal is not only marital: it is feudal. [[Medieval courtly love (fin'amor)]]

blocks.caption: Lancelot and Guinevere: the love that breaks Camelot.

blocks.text: **Mordred**, Arthur's incestuous nephew or son depending on the version, reveals the affair. Arthur condemns Guinevere to the stake. Lancelot saves her, but kills **Gawain**'s brothers in the melee. The Round Table is torn apart: civil war, end of utopia.

sections.title: The end of a world and the myth of the sleeping king

blocks.text: In **Camlann**, Arthur kills Mordred and receives a mortal wound. Excalibur is returned to the Lady of the Lake. Guinevere ends up in a convent, Lancelot a hermit. Arthur, it is said, leaves for the island of **Avalon**.
He becomes the , “former king, future king”: the sleeping king who will return at the worst time. Camelot dies in legend, and this is how it survives. [[Rex Quondam Rexque Futurus]]
**Lancelot**'s love for **Guinevere** destroys Camelot. The quest for the **Grail** only succeeds for the pure: Lancelot, the best knight, remains outside the sacred threshold.
